newsitem.title: PAKISTAN: Five said killed by Indian shelling in Kashmir.
newsitem.headline: Five said killed by Indian shelling in Kashmir.

text.p: Indian troops shelled villages in the Pakistan-controlled part of the disputed Kashmir region on Thursday, killing at least five people, Pakistan army sources said.

Four people -- two women, a girl and a man -- died in a house hit by a mortar bomb at Lawat village of the Neelum Valley, some 130 km (80 miles) northeast of Muzaffarabad, state capital of Pakistan-controlled Azad (free) Kashmir, they added.
An 11-year-old boy was killed by Indian mortar fire in the valley's Phalakan village, some 60 km (37 miles) from Muzaffarabad, the sources said.
They said Pakistani troops retaliated with heavy mortar fire on Phalakan, but there was no information about any casualties on the Indian side.

A U.N.-monitored control line separates the Indian and Pakistani armies in this Himalayan region, over which the two countries have fought two of their three wars since their independence from Britain in 1947.
Tension has run high in the region after a continuing separatist revolt by Moslem militants erupted in early 1990 in the two-thirds of Kashmir ruled by New Delhi.

Islamabad, which controls the other third, denies Indian charges of helping the revolt, and says it gives only moral and political support to what it calls "freedom-fighters" seeking independence or union with Pakistan.
